script.base: Spread and total were not saved, so this is inferred only from weeks 2-4 form and the pre-game injury report. Lamar Jackson is out, stripping Baltimore of its 12-carry/104-yard L3 QB run game. Atlanta's offense has been a run engine (Bijan Robinson 64/411, 6.42 YPC; Brian Robinson 35/163) into a Ravens defense allowing 3.93 YPC and 11 runs of 10+. Base case: Atlanta leads by halftime, stays on those two backs, and Baltimore with Tyler Huntley (only other BAL QB in the pack, 2/18 L3) trails and has to throw, with Cam Jurgens out pushing those throws shorter.
script.flip1: Huntley and Derrick Henry (65/230 L3, about 21.7 carries) keep it within a score. Atlanta cannot just clock-kill, Bijan's rush volume stays high but is not a blowout lock, and Baltimore does not fully abandon Henry, so his 80.5 rush line stays live even against a 2.99 YPC Atlanta front.
script.flip2: Jake Matthews (groin, questionable) sits or is a decoy, Atlanta's run rate collapses, and both teams throw. Bijan and Brian Robinson rush overs die, and Baltimore's quick targets (Mark Andrews 18 L3 targets, Justice Hill) rise while air-yard WRs (Rashod Bateman 178 air yards L3) do not get the deep shots the raw yardage logs imply.

injury_fallout: Source is the pre-game nflverse injury report in the pack; final inactives and practice grades are not saved. BAL QB Lamar Jackson OUT (ankle) vacates 12 carries and 104 rush yards over weeks 2-4 plus the starting dropbacks; Tyler Huntley is the inferred replacement only because he is the other BAL rusher/QB with a posted rush line (29.5), not because a starter tag was saved. BAL C Cam Jurgens OUT (concussion) and G Andrew Vorhees Q (foot) mean more pressure, worse Henry efficiency, and more quick throws (Andrews, Hill, Matthew Hibner up; deep Bateman/Devontez Walker yards down). Zay Flowers Q (foot) is not out — if he is limited, Bateman (14 targets, 171 yards L3), Walker and Andrews gain; if he plays full, that funnel does not happen. BAL LB/edge Trey Hendrickson OUT (finger) and CB Marlon Humphrey Q (hamstring) are the defensive losses Atlanta's run and, if Humphrey sits, Drake London can attack. ATL LT Jake Matthews Q (groin) is the shared kill for both Falcon rush legs. ATL DEs Za'Darius Smith Q (concussion) and Samson Ebukam Q (hamstring) would help Huntley if both sit. ATL LB Yasir Abdullah OUT (hamstring) and LB Divine Deablo Q (hamstring) are the run/TE-coverage holes, which is why a Henry under was not taken despite Atlanta allowing 2.99 YPC and only 2 runs of 10+.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack (step 4 limited). Location proxy only: ATL YPA left 6.45 on 78 attempts, middle 8.86 on 22, right 5.23 on 78. BAL YPA left 7.16 on 55, middle 8.54 on 28, right 5.34 on 53. Both defenses are tighter to the right and leak the middle on a small attempt sample.
matchup.pressure: ATL blitz rate 23%. BAL EPA/dropback vs blitz 0.39 vs 0.33 with no blitz — that split is with Lamar, not Huntley, and it predates Jurgens being out, so it cannot be used as Huntley's pressure grade. BAL blitz rate 31%. ATL EPA/dropback vs blitz 0.12 vs -0.43 when not blitzed, so Atlanta's offense has been the problem on non-blitz downs, which fits a run lean more than a Drake London ceiling game.
matchup.bleeds: ATL run defense does not bleed: 2.99 YPC and 2 runs of 10+ in 4 games, but it does bleed explosives through the air (15 passes of 20+ for 185 yards), especially the middle (8.86 YPA). BAL run defense does bleed: 3.93 YPC and 11 runs of 10+; only 12 passes of 20+ for 143, and the right side is 5.34 YPA.
matchup.overlap: The clean overlap is Bijan Robinson, the primary rusher (64 carries, 6.42 YPC in weeks 2-4), into Baltimore's explosive-run leak, with Brian Robinson (35 carries, 4.66 YPC, same three games) as the complement on that same front. Bateman's 178 air yards do not map onto Atlanta's soft middle, and the Jurgens/Vorhees profile is a quick game, so he is not a leg despite 88/37/46 vs a 17.5 line. Andrews (18 targets) vs middle-of-field and the Abdullah/Deablo absences is the pass overlap, but weeks 2-4 receiving yards resolve to 49, 24, 27 against a 31.5 line, so a lean over would be dropped.

form: Game logs are oldest-first where they sum to the L3 totals. Bijan last4 rush yards 83, 72, 194, 145; weeks 2-4 are 72+194+145=411 on 64 carries, so the recent trend is one miss (72) then 194 and 145, L3 mean 137 vs an 86.5 line. Brian Robinson last4 31, 51, 50, 62; weeks 2-4 are 51+50+62=163 on 35 carries, all three over 35.5, about 11.7 carries and 54 yards a game. Henry last4 144, 68, 89, 73; weeks 2-4 are 68+89+73=230 on 65 carries (mean 76.7 vs 80.5) but he is not a leg. London weeks 2-4 resolve to 51, 194, 96 (341 yards on 21 targets) vs 80.5 — too volatile. Bateman weeks 2-4 are 88, 37, 46. No defense-similarity splits beyond the four-game aggregates above. Penix has no prior rush games in the pack.

pro_edge.script_read: Inferred run script, not a priced one: Atlanta is the side more likely to lead and hand the ball off because Jackson is out and BAL allows 3.93 YPC with 11 runs of 10+, while ATL's own rush defense (2.99 YPC) can stall Henry. If that lead is real, Bijan and Brian Robinson carries go up late and Baltimore's WR/TE targets go up only if Huntley is chasing. A low-total, run-heavy lean is the read; a shootout flip cuts both rush legs together.

Bijan rushyds over 86.5 best saved price -119 at a consensus no-vig over of 0.511 (fair is about a coin flip, -119 does not beat it). Brian Robinson rushyds over 35.5 best -112 vs no-vig over 0.497. pro_edge.lagging: Bateman recyds 17.5 is still a 0.499/0.501 coin flip against weeks 2-4 yards of 88, 37 and 46. That looks lagging only if the market ignored his role; it may already be the Jackson-out reprice, so it is not a bet. Henry 80.5 (no-vig over 0.502) and Hill rush 11.5 (no-vig over 0.497) are also still coin flips after 104 vacated Jackson rush yards — those lines may not have moved. Walker over is the one juiced number (-120, no-vig over 0.512) with Flowers only questionable.
pro_edge.sleepers: Out: Lamar Jackson (ankle), Cam Jurgens (concussion), Trey Hendrickson (finger), Yasir Abdullah (hamstring). Jackson has no same-position QB teammate in the rush/rec prop list; the vacated 12/104 rush yards point at Henry and Hill, whose lines have not shortened or lengthened off 50/50 — sleeper candidates only, rejected because ATL allows 2.99 YPC and the center is out. Abdullah out and Deablo questionable would sleeper BAL TE/RB overs (Andrews 31.5, Hibner 6.5, Henry 80.5); those lines are still ~50/50 and were not taken. Flowers is questionable, not out, so Walker and Bateman are not confirmed sleepers. Penix rushyds 1 has no two-sided price and no prior games; fallback.py was not run.

data_check.notes: No sim file, no projection model and no Pinnacle number were in the pack, so step 8 cannot confirm a median or a sharp no-vig. Box scores agree with both leans: Bijan L3 mean 137 vs 86.5, Brian Robinson 51/50/62 vs 35.5, and BAL's 3.93 YPC / 11 explosive runs agree. Prices disagree with a value bet — both best overs are juiced past a ~50% consensus no-vig — so these are sized as leans, not price edges. Passed Bateman over 17.5 because the average-versus-line gap is exactly the averages trap: Jurgens out and ATL outside YPA (left 6.45, right 5.23) disagree with a vertical-WR over, so the lean is dropped rather than flagged as strong. Passed Huntley rush over 29.5 (only 18 yards in the pack, no starter sample), Flowers under 68.5 (questionable, may not play; log shows 150/84/118 but L3 aggregate is 202), Andrews over 31.5 (24 and 27 under the line), London over/under 80.5 (51-yard week inside a 194), and Hill markets (rush last4 18, 6, 33, 3).

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both rush overs lost because it was one story and the story broke. Matthews was inactive or a non-factor, Atlanta could not run on early downs, and Baltimore — even without Hendrickson — loaded the box because Huntley never punished the non-blitz looks that have already graded at -0.43 EPA per dropback for Atlanta. Bijan posted another week-2-style 72 under 86.5, and Brian Robinson was the back who got capped once the carries consolidated or the game flipped to throws. The -119 and -112 prices had no cushion, the 194- and 145-yard Bijan games were the variance not the median, and with no saved total there was no check against a defensive slog. That shared kill is stronger than either leg alone, which is why both stay leans and not strong.
slip_story: One Atlanta run-control stack: Bijan rushyds over 86.5 with Brian Robinson rushyds over 35.5. They win together if Atlanta leads and keeps the committee that just produced 64 and 35 carries in three games against a Ravens defense leaking runs of 10+. Do not add a total under, a Henry over, or Baltimore receiving overs — those need the pass flip or the stacked-box flip this slip is fading. No TDs. Nothing is placed; this is a pre-kick log only.
